verdict.rationale: Galileo's docs say users can extend out-of-the-box metrics with custom LLM-as-a-judge metrics, and a dedicated cookbook covers creating them for domain-specific evaluation. Those metrics can then score experiments. Configurability goes further: metrics can be global or project-scoped, and natural-language feedback auto-tunes them. Missing for 10: detailed documentation of judge configuration options (judge model selection, prompt/rubric specifics, output scales), and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an ML engineer, I can score outputs with configurable LLM-as-a-judge evaluators

citations.quote: You can then expand these metrics with custom metrics, using LLM-as-a-judge, or custom code-based metrics.
Learn how to create custom LLM-as-a-Judge metrics to evaluate domain-specific applications within Galileo.
This allows you to continuously provide feedback in natural language that automatically improves the metrics to align better with your domain, or expected inputs and outputs.
Choose whether a metric is global and available in every project, or project-scoped and available in selected projects.
Experiments allow you to evaluate prompts, models, and your application code, using well-defined inputs, against metrics of your choice.
